title: NCLAT Holds Tata Capital's Hypothecated Assets Fall Into Liquidation Estate for Missing 30-Day Window
case_name: Tata Capital Limited v. Sanjay Mahajan (Liquidator)
card_summary: NCLAT Delhi dismissed Tata Capital's appeal seeking to pull hypothecated assets out of a liquidation estate. Tata Capital's Form D claim marked the security-interest column nil, and its first clear written election to realise security outside the estate came six months after liquidation began. The Tribunal held a pending Section 230 scheme does not extend the 30-day window under Section 52.
card_tip: File Form D accurately and send a written election to realise security within 30 days of liquidation commencement; a pending compromise scheme is no excuse to wait.
verification_notes: Confirmed across Taxscan, TaxGuru and Fox Mandal, which agree on the appeal number, the 6 October 2026 dismissal, the nil entry against security interest in Form D, the 19 February 2025 election letter being too late, and the holding that Section 230 proceedings do not toll the Section 52 timeline. Did not independently verify against the NCLAT order itself, which was not located on the tribunal's own site.
